organizations.normalization_notes: Harvard's academic professorship is recorded separately from the directorship of the Harvard-Yenching Institute. Neither role is inferred from education or alumni status.

organizations.organization_type: independent research institute affiliated with Harvard University
organizations.normalization_notes: Kept separate from Harvard University: institutional sources distinguish appointment as Institute director from the Harvard professorship.
The 1934 Harvard Crimson describes the institution as 'of the University of Paris'; this historical phrasing is retained in the citation, not silently substituted for the named school.

affiliations.date_precision: Harvard gives the effective appointment date as 1 September 1934 and documents an active Harvard career spanning World War II; no individual OSS start date or intervening employer has been established
affiliations.research_notes: The 1934 Harvard professorship clearly predates wartime consulting. It appears to have continued during the war, so it is not labeled as a job he left immediately before OSS, nor as the last civilian job before military service.

affiliations.date_precision: Harvard records appointment in November 1933, effective during 1934; the Institute records a 1934–56 directorship, overlapping the war
affiliations.research_notes: Separate institutional appointment, concurrent with his Harvard professorship. Exact OSS relationship and chronology require Box 216 review.

affiliations.date_precision: A February 1934 contemporary notice says he had held a professorship since February 1930; a January 1934 notice identifies him as Director of Studies in Paris in the 1933–34 academic year. Exact end date is not established.
affiliations.research_notes: Contemporary reports document this earlier Paris academic role. His later Harvard appointment intervened before wartime OSS-related work.

claims.claim_text: The person indexed as Dr. Sergei Elisseeff is strongly identified with Serge Elisséeff, appointed professor of Far Eastern Languages at Harvard University effective 1 September 1934; the professorship preceded and overlapped his wartime U.S. government consulting.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard's departmental chronology gives the 1934 professorial appointment. Its biography describes the academic career, and the Harvard-Yenching Institute identifies the Sergei/Serge name variants and wartime consulting.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High, not confirmed: the uncommon indexed surname, given-name variant, and Dr. title align with Harvard's named professor; the Institute explicitly equates Sergei Grigorievich Eliseev and Serge Elisséeff and describes wartime U.S. government consulting. The Box 216 file has not been examined.
claims.temporal_assessment: Appointment effective in 1934, before OSS existed; the institutional role continued into the war. No evidence establishes that Harvard was an employer he left immediately for OSS.
claims.match_notes: This is employment, not Harvard student status. It is an earlier/concurrent role, not a proven immediate predecessor or last civilian employer before service.

claims.claim_text: Elisséeff became director of the Harvard-Yenching Institute in 1934, a position the Institute documents through 1956; this role preceded and overlapped his wartime government consulting.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Institute's institutional account dates his directorship 1934–56, while Harvard's chronology documents the original appointment and separates it from his professorship.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High for the same rare-name, title, and wartime-consulting crosswalk; no original Box 216 personnel file has yet been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The directorship began before OSS and continued during the war; it cannot be treated as an organization he left to join OSS.
claims.match_notes: The independent Institute is not silently collapsed into Harvard University. Government consulting is a separate wartime activity, not a named pre-OSS employer claim.

claims.claim_text: Before his permanent Harvard appointment, Elisséeff held a professorship at the École pratique des hautes études in Paris from February 1930 and was its Director of Studies during the 1933–34 academic year.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two Harvard Crimson announcements in January and February 1934 document the Paris institution, role, and chronology before his September Harvard appointment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: the two contemporary notices identify the same uncommon-name scholar and Harvard appointee, linked to the indexed Dr. Sergei Elisseeff through Harvard-Yenching's Sergei/Serge name crosswalk and wartime consultant account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented in 1930 and 1933–34; certainly before OSS. Harvard appointments intervened, so this was not the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.match_notes: Named teaching institution and role are documented directly; the cited 1934 notices do not establish the precise end of the Paris appointment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: NARA's rare indexed name and Dr. title match institutional accounts of Professor Serge Elisséeff. Harvard-Yenching explicitly equates Sergei Grigorievich Eliseev with Serge Elisséeff and documents wartime U.S. government consulting. This is a strong biographical match, not direct inspection of Box 216.
person_updates.next_action: Review NARA RG 226 Entry A1-224 Box 216 and the cited OSS-era memo to establish the actual consultant assignment, dates, and whether any distinct immediate pre-OSS affiliation existed.
